options.label: Zignoruj — produkty startują bez labelek (Recommended)

questions.question: Jak określić kontekst widoku (project vs product)? Topbar nie dostaje wprost informacji o typie wyświetlanych elementów.

options.label: Z bieżącego item (route) (Recommended)
options.description: Topbar odczytuje item z aktualnego URL i sprawdza allowedChildTypes — jeśli dzieckiem jest project to kontekst projektowy, jeśli product to produktowy.

options.description: Ukryj atrybuty specyficzne dla jednego typu — wyświetlaj tylko te, które mają allowedTypes obejmujące oba typy.

questions.question: What should happen to existing labels when we split them?

options.label: Migrate existing (Recommended)
options.description: Add a one-time migration step that moves existing label items to the appropriate new type (project-labels or product-labels). Requires user to decide which existing labels go where.

options.label: Start fresh
options.description: Keep existing label items untouched (they become orphaned/unused), and create new empty containers for project-labels and product-labels.

options.label: Copy to both
options.description: Duplicate existing label items into both the project-labels container and the product-labels container.

questions.question: Should we introduce new item types (project-label, product-label) or reuse the existing 'label' type with separate relation keys and containers?

options.label: New item types (Recommended)
options.description: Create ItemTypes.projectLabel and ItemTypes.productLabel. Cleanly separates the two label namespaces at the type level. More future-proof.

options.label: Same type, new relations
options.description: Keep ItemTypes.label but add RelationKeys.projectLabels and RelationKeys.productLabels. Simpler change but less strict separation.

questions.question: Which UI components show labels, and do you want both label menus to look and behave the same way?

options.label: Same behavior (Recommended)
options.description: Both project-label and product-label menus work identically to the current LabelMenu.vue, just filtered to their respective label type.

options.label: Different behavior
options.description: The two menus should differ in some way (e.g., product labels use a different widget, or have different ordering). I will describe how in the 'Other' field.

questions.question: Should tasks/notes (leaf items) inherit labels from their parent project or product, or only projects/products themselves get labeled?

options.label: Only projects & products
options.description: Labels apply only to project/product items. Tasks and notes are not directly labeled.

options.label: Leaf items too (current behavior)
options.description: Keep existing behavior where tasks and notes can also be labeled directly, with the new split label types.

answers.What should happen to existing labels wh: existing labels should be used for projects, and new type created for products

Should we introduce new item types (proj.notes: only one new type and relation (for products)

questions.question: Should project labels and product labels be completely separate lists (users manage them independently), or is there any overlap where the same label could apply to both types?

options.label: Completely separate (Recommended)
options.description: Project labels and product labels are two independent lists. A 'priority' label for projects and a 'priority' label for products are different items.

options.label: Shared pool
options.description: All labels come from one shared list, but each item type can use a different subset. Fewer labels to manage, but no type-scoping.

questions.question: What relation key name should be used for product labels in the code?

options.label: productLabels (Recommended)
options.description: Consistent with existing naming: productType, productStatus, productLabels.

options.description: Product labels are called 'tags' in the UI and codebase.

options.label: Other
options.description: You'll specify a different name.

questions.question: Should the filter panel be updated to have separate label filters for projects and products?

options.label: Yes — separate filter rows (Recommended)

options.label: No — keep one label filter
options.description: The label filter row stays as-is but only shows labels relevant to the current view context.

options.label: No — tasks/notes get no labels

questions.question: How should product labels be implemented?

options.label: New ItemType (Recommended)
options.description: Add a new ItemType (e.g. 'productLabel') and a new RelationKey (e.g. 'productLabels'). Clean separation mirroring how productStatus/productType differ from status/label.

questions.question: What happens to existing label data on products when we make this change?

options.label: Keep as-is (no migration)
options.description: Existing product-label assignments stay under the old 'labels' relation and are effectively lost/ignored going forward. Clean break, simple implementation.

options.label: Migrate existing data
options.description: Write a migration script to move existing product label relationships to the new 'productLabels' relation. More work but preserves data.

options.label: Products have no labels yet
options.description: Products don't actually have any labels assigned yet, so no migration is needed.
